wal: understand what an explanation text is and how it differs from a narrative
tib: This is so I know the features I need to include when I plan and write this week.
isb: reading the model text and identifying what the writer does differently to a story writer.

title: Grammar Warm-Up
subtitle: Story, instructions or explanation? Decide which genre each extract belongs to.

cards.label: Extract A
lines: Varjak crept forward.
His paws made no sound.
The darkness pressed around him.
Which genre?

cards.label: Extract B
lines: First, find a safe shadow.
Next, press your body low.
Then wait until the danger passes.
Which genre?

cards.label: Extract C
lines: Slow-Time works by calming
the mind. As a result, danger
seems to move more slowly.
Which genre?

title: Back to Varjak’s world.
lines: Remember Jalal and the Seven Skills of the Way of Jalal.
Re-read the sections where Jalal teaches each skill.
Think about this:
•  Who needs to know this information?
•  Why would a house cat new to the city need it?
•  What is the most important thing they should understand?
Talk to your partner. Which skill do you think matters most?

title: A new kind of writing.
lines: We have spent two weeks writing a narrative.
This week we are writing an explanation text.
An explanation text:
•  tells you HOW and WHY something works
•  is written in the present tense
•  uses a formal, clear register
•  has subheadings to organise sections
•  links ideas using causal connectives
A story shows events. An explanation explains processes.

title: Reading the model text.
left_lines: Uses a subheading for each skill
Explains how and why in present tense
Uses connectives to show cause and effect
right_label: Look for this in our model

lines: Read the model text together.
Discuss these three questions:
1.  Why does the writer open with a question instead of a statement?
What effect does this have on the reader?
2.  Pick one skill section. How does the writer show both
WHAT the skill is AND WHY it helps?
3.  What is different about reading this compared to reading
the chapters from Varjak Paw?
Be ready to share your best point with the class.

q1: What was the trickiest difference to spot between a narrative and an explanation text?
q2: Why does an explanation text use the present tense instead of the past tense?
q3: Which part of the model text would you most like to try in your own writing?
